presGrad_:
Perform dimensional analysis for turbulent boundary layers under pressure gradient effects to derive the dimensionless form of the friction velocity (denoted as U_tau/U_inf). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 6 dimensional physical quantities as input parameters: 
the free-stream velocity (U_inf), the kinematic viscosity (nu), the integrated mean-flow kinetic energy (MKE, defined by the integral: ∫(0 to delta) U^2 dy), the boundary layer thickness at 99% of free-stream (delta), the boundary layer displacement thickness (delta*), and the boundary layer momentum thickness (theta).
laser_material:
Perform dimensional analysis for laser-melted liquid metal to derive the dimensionless form of the keyhole depth (denoted as e*). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 7 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the material density (ρ), the temperature difference between melting temperature and ambient temperature (Tl − T0), the laser beam radius (r0), and the thermal diffusivity (α), the effective laser power (ηP), the heat capacity (cp), the laser scan speed (Vs).
mhd_generator:
Perform dimensional analysis for a magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) generator to derive the dimensionless form of the average flow velocity (denoted as u*). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 6 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the side length of the square duct (h), the dynamic viscosity (μ), the fluid density (ρ), the electrical resistivity of the fluid (η), the applied pressure gradient (dp/dx), and the magnetic field magnitude (B).
rayleigh_benard:
Perform dimensional analysis for Rayleigh-Bénard convection in a planar horizontal layer of fluid heated from below, to derive the dimensionless form of the Nusselt number (denoted as Nu). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 7 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the height of the container (h), the thermal conductivity (lambda), the temperature difference between the top and bottom surfaces (delta_T), the gravitational acceleration (g), the thermal expansion coefficient (alpha), the kinematic viscosity (nu), and the thermal diffusivity (kappa).
blasius_:
Perform dimensional analysis for the Blasius laminar boundary layer over a flat plate to derive the dimensionless form of the streamwise velocity (denoted as u*). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 4 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the free-stream velocity (U), the kinematic viscosity (nu), the streamwise distance from the leading edge (x), and the wall-normal distance (y).
velotrans_compTurb:
Perform dimensional analysis for compressible wall-bounded channel turbulence to derive the dimensionless form of the normalized mean velocity (denoted as u+). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 6 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the wall-normal distance (y), the wall density (ρ_w), the wall dynamic viscosity (μ_w), the fluid density (ρ), the dynamic viscosity (μ), and the friction velocity (u_tau). 
Due to incomplete similarity, the output variable needs to be scaled. To ensure comparability with the log-law and uniqueness of results, the power of wall units must be constrained to 1 for the INPUT and 0 for the OUTPUT formula.
goldenfeld_:
Perform dimensional analysis for rough-wall turbulent pipe flow to derive the dimensionless form of the friction factor (denoted as cf). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 5 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the fluid density (ρ), the dynamic viscosity (μ), the pipe diameter (D), the flow velocity (U), and the pipe wall roughness height (r). 
Due to incomplete similarity, the output variable needs to be scaled. To ensure uniqueness of results, the power of relative roughness height must be constrained to 0 for the OUTPUT formula.
laminar_mvp_:
Perform dimensional analysis for laminar Newtonian channel flow in pressure drop coordinates to derive the dimensionless form of the mean velocity (denoted as u+). 
This analysis uses ONLY the following 4 physical quantities as input parameters: 
the friction velocity (u_tau), the fluid kinematic viscosity (nu), the wall-normal distance (y), and the channel half-length (delta). 
Due to incomplete similarity, the output variable needs to be scaled. To ensure uniqueness of results, the power of the wall units must be constrained to 0 for the OUTPUT formula.
CMAME24_CESS_PROMPT:
Perform dimensional analysis for the Cess eddy-viscosity model in turbulent channel flow to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the normalized eddy viscosity (denoted as nu_t/nu).
This analysis uses ONLY the following 4 dimensional physical quantities as input parameters:
the channel half-height (h), the distance from the wall (y), the friction velocity (u_tau), and the fluid kinematic viscosity (nu).
CMAME24_PIPE_PROMPT:
Perform dimensional analysis for viscous flow in a rough circular pipe to derive the dimensionless relationship governing the pipe friction factor (denoted as f_D).
This analysis uses ONLY the following 5 dimensional physical quantities as input parameters:
the fluid density (rho), the dynamic viscosity (mu), the pipe diameter (D), the mean flow velocity (U), and the absolute wall roughness height (epsilon).
